title: Plant hazards, guarding and exclusion zones
audience: Cleaners working near industrial plant, machinery and conveyors where degreasing is requested.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish ordinary walkways from guarded, moving, elevated, hot and restricted machinery zones.
Recognise that an unguarded machine is a stop, regardless of a request to hurry.
Record the concern and refer to the responsible supervisor and competent plant specialist.

instruction.heading: Reading the machinery zones
instruction.body: On an industrial site, machinery creates zones: ordinary walkways, guarded areas, moving parts, elevated platforms, hot surfaces and restricted areas. A floor plan shows these zones, and the site decides who may enter each. Check the plan before you move, and do not assume that a zone is open because it looks quiet.

instruction.heading: Guarding is a stop
instruction.body: A guard is there to keep people away from moving or dangerous parts. If a guard is missing, damaged or bypassed, the machine is not safe to clean near. Under the national plant code, guards have to go back on before plant restarts after maintenance, and plant should not be run with its guarding removed (instrument dated 17 December 2015). A supervisor who says that the cleaning can proceed quickly despite an unguarded conveyor is asking you to work in a stop condition. Refuse, withdraw, and record the request. Any worker may stop unsafe work where they reasonably fear serious harm from an immediate or imminent hazard (Commonwealth WHS Act section 84, compilation dated 1 July 2024).

instruction.heading: What a cleaner records and refers
instruction.body: Record the equipment or location identifier, the observed concern, the source of the evidence, the people notified and the immediate restriction. Say what is unknown. Ask the responsible supervisor to assign the competent plant specialist. A cleaner does not sign off plant as safe. This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or fire-safety approval, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

procedure: Read the floor plan and identify guarded, moving, elevated, hot and restricted zones.
Do not enter a restricted or guarded zone without the site's documented authority.
Treat a missing or bypassed guard as a stop, and withdraw.
Record the equipment or location, the concern, the source, the people notified and the restriction.
Refer to the supervisor and the competent plant specialist, and do not sign off plant.

workedExamples.situation: A production supervisor points to an unguarded conveyor and says the cleaning can proceed quickly.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not proceed. An unguarded conveyor is a stop condition, and speed is not authority. Withdraw from the conveyor zone, record the concern and the supervisor's request, and ask the responsible supervisor to assign a competent plant specialist before any cleaning.

equipmentAndPpe: Site floor plan and zone map.
High-visibility clothing as the site requires.
Record form for concerns and restrictions.

commonErrors.error: Working faster because a supervisor asks.
commonErrors.prevention: Speed is not authority. Stop on an unguarded machine.

commonErrors.error: Stepping inside a guarded zone to reach a corner.
commonErrors.prevention: Stay out of guarded zones unless documented authority is given.

commonErrors.error: Signing off a machine as safe.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the concern. A competent plant specialist decides.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Plant guarding and machinery safety are covered by work health and safety duties, and the person who manages or controls the plant holds those duties (instrument dated 17 December 2015).
This lesson does not grant a licence, competency or environmental authority for industrial degreasing.
This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or fire-safety approval, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

Referral to the supervisor and competent plant specialist.
summary: Read the zone map and keep out of restricted zones.
An unguarded machine is a stop.
Record and refer; do not sign off plant.

knowledgeChecks.question: A supervisor says to clean the area quickly beside an unguarded conveyor. What is correct?
options: Do not proceed; withdraw, record and refer to the competent plant specialist
Clean quickly, since the supervisor asked and the job has to be done today
Clean but avoid the guard for now, since the guard is in the way of the work

knowledgeChecks.question: What does a guard do?
options: Decorates the machine and makes it look neat
Keeps people away from moving or dangerous parts
Stops the machine when someone walks past the area

knowledgeChecks.question: Who decides that a machine is safe to clean near?
options: The cleaner, who is closest to the machine and sees it daily
The first operator, who starts the machine each morning
The competent plant specialist and the responsible supervisor
